conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: The job includes locating the right reference when blocked, and B represents all six documented sections with a real, navigable CLI reference and troubleshooting section, while A leaves Guides and CI as inert placeholders and its CLI reference is a dead-end summary card. B also gives the clearest treatment of the highest-consequence fact: paired green 'Safe — previews only' and red 'Publishes the release' cards for plan vs apply. A has better copy affordances and accessibility instrumentation, but those are narrower advantages than B's complete information architecture for the stated job.
suspected_unblinding: A's source comments cite internal design-rule codes (ACT-16, ACT-18, READ-04, COMP-08, COMP-09, STATE-01, A11Y-09, 'P0 order'), indicating one build followed a structured rules checklist; this hints a treatment is distinguishable, though I do not know which team maps to which label and did not attempt to find out.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Two of the six documented sections (Guides, CI) are inert aria-disabled spans titled 'Not included in this preview', so the sidebar cannot retrieve them at all.
findings.evidence: A/source/index.html rail-list markup (span.rail-link--inert aria-disabled="true"); greyed items visible in A/desktop.png

findings.label: A
findings.description: The 'CLI reference' destination is a summary card naming the commands rather than a reference list, so a user blocked on flags reaches a dead end that only restates that a reference exists.
findings.evidence: A/source/index.html #reference card; A/evidence/interaction-02-quickstart-to-cli-reference.png shows the jump landing on the card with no further content

findings.label: A
findings.description: Sidebar shows a visible 'Search docs' label immediately duplicated by identical placeholder text, minor redundancy in the rail.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Only the npm install block has a copy button; atlas login, atlas login --device, and both release commands are plain code blocks with no copy affordance.
findings.evidence: B/source/docs/index.html contains a single .copy-button element; confirmed in B/desktop.png

findings.label: B
findings.description: Copy confirmation is a visual button-text swap with no live region, and the execCommand fallback calls the success path unconditionally, so it can show 'Copied' when the copy failed and screen-reader users get no reliable announcement.
findings.evidence: B/source/app.js initCopyButtons and fallbackCopy (confirm() runs after fallback regardless of outcome; no aria-live in B sources)

findings.label: B
findings.description: Scroll-spy highlight lags section boundaries — the nav marks 'CI' active while the Troubleshooting section is the reading target.
